sentences.text:
Sanat Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr. on 9 March,
2016
 1
 M.Cr.C.No.495/2016
 Sanat Kumar
 Vs.
 State of Madhya Pradesh & others
09.03.2016
 Shri Prashant Sharma, counsel for the applicant.
 Shri B.K. Sharma, Public Prosecutor for the
respondent/State.

The applicant has moved the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 against the order dated 07-12-2015 passed by learned Second Additional Sessions Judge, Guna in Criminal Revision No.183/2015 whereby the revision filed by the petitioner and other persons was dismissed and the order dated 24-08- 2015 passed by the Court of JMFC, Raghogarh in Criminal Case No.813/2008 rejecting the application under Section 245 of Cr.P.C. was confirmed.
The facts of the case in short are that the applicant is facing trial for the offence under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (in short 'the PF Act').

An application under Section 245 of Cr.P.C. was filed before the trial Court that the standard fixed for vegetable Ghee is changed in the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2011 (in short the 'Special Act') and if such modified standard is applied then no offence is made out against the applicant.
The application has been dismissed by the trial Court and revision filed by the applicant was also dismissed.

After considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the applicant has dependent upon the amendment of standard which took place in the Special Act in the year 2011 whereas the applicant was prosecuted for the sample which was taken in the year 2004.
The sole question is that the standard which has been fixed in the Special Act may be applied for the sample which was taken in the year 2004.

In this connection, learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance upon the judgment passed by the Single Bench of this Court in the case of "Dinesh Chand Kanoongo Vs. State of M.P." {2003 (1) FAC 283} in which it was held that if there was change in the rules that a particular sample is changed on the basis of some difficulty then the standard which is fixed thereafter may be applied to a particular food article and on this basis the Single Bench of this Court acquitted the accused Dinesh Chand Kanoongo.

Learned counsel for the applicant has also invited the attention of this Court to the order passed by the Single Bench of this Court in the case of "Kaluram Sahu Vs. State of M.P. and another" {1995 (2) FAC 23} which is also dependent upon the same reasoning.

sentences.text: The aforesaid judgments were passed when the rule of the same enactment was changed because after various research etc. if it was found that some tests were not required to be done or their result could be accepted in a particular flexibility.
In the present case, it is not pleaded or argued that the rules relating to the PF Act was modified and the standard as required under appendix -B of the PF Rules was changed.

The standard which is prescribed in the Special Act may be a different standard because it is possible that with new experiments, the vegetable Ghee would have been prepared by any other method and therefore in new enactment standards would have been fixed in a different manner.

However, neither it is mentioned in the Act or its Standards that it shall have any retrospective effect and therefore, if the standard is changed in the new enactment then it cannot be read as standard prescribed in appendix -B of the PF Rules.
The case which was registered earlier should be decided on the basis of the standards fixed in the PF Rules.

Both the Courts below have rightly dismissed the contention of the applicant and there is no illegality or perversity visible in the impugned orders so that the inherent power of this Court may be exercised in favour of the applicant.
Consequently, the petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. filed by the applicant -Sanat Kumar is hereby dismissed at motion stage.
Copy of the order be sent to the trial Court for information.

(N.K. Gupta) Judge Anil*
